memories.memory_text: I was told by Reese Wilder that each Moon is a separate kingdom, hostile to the others, and that the only thing they share is Micah Hale's rule and their hatred of him — and that the Sand Men are part of this.

memories.memory_text: I made a sudden move on the control panel, forcing the craft into a violent dive because I knew it was the only way to take control.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne physically restrains Reese Wilder by seizing her wrists as she attempts to regain control of the craft.
memories.memory_text: I seized Reese Wilder's wrists when she tried to reach for the controls, holding her back so I could maintain control of the craft.

grounded_facts: The spacecraft is descending rapidly toward the surface of Ardentia, posing immediate danger.
memories.memory_text: I saw the surface of Ardentia looming up fast while I held Reese Wilder, knowing we were diving straight toward it and there was no time to waste.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne physically restrains Reese Wilder and demands she place the mind control device on him to contact Jonah Vale.

memories.memory_text: I grabbed Reese Wilder and demanded she put the mind control device on me to connect with Jonah Vale, holding her wrists tight as she struggled.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne suddenly reaches out to Jonah Vale, asking if she senses his presence.

memories.memory_text: I reached out to Jonah Vale with my filtered voice, asking if she could sense me, breaking into her moment unexpectedly.

grounded_facts: After hearing Tristan Hawthorne, Jonah Vale blinks and declares that she must be dreaming, indicating a shift in her perception of the situation.

memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Vale blink and pause, then heard her say 'I'm dreaming,' after I spoke, as if she couldn't believe I was really reaching her.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne uses the Thought Transference device to mentally communicate with Jonah Vale, asserting their connection across distance.
Tristan Hawthorne mentally communicates with Jonah Vale to confirm his presence and dispel any doubt that their connection is real.
memories.memory_text: I used the Thought Transference device to reach Jonah Vale in her mind, focusing hard to make the connection, and I told her, 'No, Jonah Vale -- you're not dreaming, I'm Tristan Hawthorne -- I'm with you and you are with me!' to make sure she knew it was really me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne reaches out mentally to Jonah Vale, testing and confirming the connection.

Jonah Vale responds mentally to Tristan Hawthorne, confirming she is receiving his thoughts.
memories.memory_text: I reached out mentally to Jonah Vale, asking if she was receiving my thoughts, and when she confirmed she was, I realized we had established a two-way telepathic link—I could hear her and she could hear me.

grounded_facts: A covert telepathic interaction between Tristan Hawthorne and Jonah Vale occurring while Jonah Vale is being bathed by Shawn Vale and other females.
memories.memory_text: I think I communicated with Jonah Vale while she was being bathed by Shawn Vale and the others, though I'm not sure if they noticed—I sensed it might have been hidden from them.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne informs Jonah Vale that he is traveling to the Kingdom of Arboria in a spacecraft with Reese Wilder, Micah Hale's daughter, to seek help.
memories.memory_text: I informed Jonah Vale that I was traveling to the Kingdom of Arboria in a spacecraft with Reese Wilder, Micah Hale's daughter, to seek help.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale insists that Reese Wilder means nothing to Tristan Hawthorne, affirming emotional exclusivity.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Reese Wilder means nothing to me and that my loyalty belongs only to Jonah Vale, who insists on emotional exclusivity.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne reacts with alarm upon hearing Jonah Vale is with Reese Wilder, calling her a 'bitch' and warning not to trust her.
memories.memory_text: I reacted with alarm when I heard Jonah Vale was with Reese Wilder, calling Reese Wilder a 'bitch' and warning Jonah Vale not to trust her.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale discloses being naked in a bathtub, under preparation for Micah Hale, with Tristan Quincy imprisoned.
memories.memory_text: Jonah Vale told me she was naked in a bathtub, being prepared for Micah Hale, and that Tristan Quincy was chained in a dungeon — I heard the fear in her voice and felt helpless not being able to reach her.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale acknowledges the difficulty but agrees to follow Tristan Hawthorne's instructions to survive and escape.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jonah Vale acknowledge how tough the mission would be, but she agreed to follow my instructions to survive and escape.

grounded_facts: A real-time voice exchange between Tristan Hawthorne in a spacecraft and Jonah Vale in captivity, used to share critical information and coordinate resistance.
memories.memory_text: I was in the spacecraft with Reese Wilder, speeding toward the Kingdom of Arboria to get help, and I told Jonah Vale over our voice link that I’d find her — I could hear her voice but couldn’t see or touch her, and I urged her to stay strong and fake out Micah Hale’s forces until I could return.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne tells Jonah Vale to deceive Micah Hale's forces and free Tristan Quincy while promising future rescue.
memories.memory_text: I told Jonah Vale to fake out Micah Hale's forces and get to Tristan Quincy so she could free him, and I promised her I'd find her and help would come.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne expresses longing and romantic commitment, implying shared thoughts and future reunion.
memories.memory_text: I told Jonah Vale we're going to get out of this jam, and I'll find her — I swore it, and I meant it, because I can't stop thinking about our future together.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder abruptly removes the Thought Transfer bubble from Tristan Hawthorne's head, ending his mental engagement.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Reese Wilder abruptly removes the Thought Transfer bubble from Tristan Hawthorne's head, ending his mental engagement.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Reese Wilder forcibly takes the Thought Transfer bubble from Tristan Hawthorne's head, interrupting his mental connection or experience.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder slaps Tristan Hawthorne to snap him out of his dazed, dreamy state after removing the Thought Transfer bubble.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Reese Wilder slaps Tristan Hawthorne to snap him out of his dazed, dreamy state after removing the Thought Transfer bubble.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder slaps Tristan Hawthorne and verbally directs his attention to Arboria.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Reese Wilder slaps Tristan Hawthorne and verbally directs his attention to Arboria.

memories.memory_text: I was told that After snapping Tristan Hawthorne out of his trance, Reese Wilder points ahead and announces the sighting of Arboria.

memories.memory_text: I was frantically working the controls as greenery rushed by outside, then suddenly we crashed—THUMP, THUD, CRASH—the craft jolted to a halt and nearly knocked the wind out of me and Reese Wilder.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne acknowledges his failure in landing the craft and apologizes.
memories.memory_text: I admitted to Reese Wilder that I was sorry and that landings aren't my thing after I messed up the landing.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Wilder exit the shuttle craft that is trapped in a giant vine, beginning their descent to the forest below.
memories.memory_text: I struggled out of the shuttle and helped Reese Wilder up, then knelt on the cabin to take in the incredible vista around us as we began our descent along the giant vine.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne makes a cultural reference to 'Robin Hood' and asks Reese Wilder about his location, which she does not understand.
memories.memory_text: I made a joke about Robin Hood and asked Reese Wilder where he was, but she just responded with 'Who?'—I realized she didn't get the reference.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder tells Tristan Hawthorne to follow her as she begins moving along the vine trunk, establishing leadership in navigation.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Reese Wilder to follow her as she started moving carefully along the trunk of the great vine, balancing lithely ahead of me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne pauses and questions whether Drew Prescott will help him, showing doubt about the plan or alliance.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Tristan Hawthorne pauses and questions whether Drew Prescott will help him, showing doubt about the plan or alliance.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder gently but provocatively places her finger on Tristan Hawthorne's lips to silence him, urging trust.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Reese Wilder gently but provocatively places her finger on Tristan Hawthorne's lips to silence him, urging trust.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder tells Tristan Hawthorne to be quiet and trust her after he questions Drew Prescott's help.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Reese Wilder tells Tristan Hawthorne to be quiet and trust her after he questions Drew Prescott's help.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne recognizes the structure of Arboria as something he dreamed of in childhood, indicating a personal connection to the place.
memories.memory_text: I remember saying out loud that I dreamed of this tree-house when I was a kid, because the structure of Arboria felt so familiar.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder identifies the sounds from the forest as Drew Prescott's hunt and warns Tristan Hawthorne to watch, signaling the presence of an ongoing event.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Wilder tell me, 'It's Drew Prescott's hunt! Watch!' when the forest sounds started.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder physically leads Tristan Hawthorne upward in response to the sounds, guiding him to a vantage point.
memories.memory_text: I was with Reese Wilder when the forest erupted in cries and roars, and she led me quickly up the spiral stairs to a balcony so I could see what was happening.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Wilder arrive at and begin ascending the structure of Arboria, marking their entry into a significant location.
memories.memory_text: I was climbing the spiral stairs with Reese Wilder, and then she led me quickly up to a wide balcony as the forest filled with strange cries and roaring sounds.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne asks Reese Wilder whether the shouting group will genuinely help him.
memories.memory_text: I asked Reese Wilder directly, 'These are the guys who are gonna help me?' because I needed to know if they were truly on my side.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne expresses doubt about the Crown Hill Medical Center who are supposed to help him, reacting to their shouting.
memories.memory_text: I heard the shouting and my eyes jumped to Reese Wilder, doubting whether these Crown Hill Medical Center would really help me.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder clarifies that the shouting is not genuine support but a result of political pressure.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Reese Wilder that the shouting means nothing—that they only do it because it's treason not to, and that they hate Micah Hale.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott senses the presence of the Reese Prescott near the lodge and commands the Eastwood Collective to form battle lines.
Drew Prescott issues orders to the Eastwood Collective to form battle lines in preparation for combat.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Prescott shout that he scented a Reese Prescott near the lodge, and then I saw him command the Eastwood Collective to form battle lines above and below.

grounded_facts: The Reese Prescott silently directs the crouching Bennett Delaney to retreat while he covers their escape.

memories.memory_text: I saw the Reese Prescott watch the crouching Bennett Delaney, then signal them to retreat before he charged the Eastwood Collective alone—I could feel his rage as he threw himself into the fight.

grounded_facts: The Nico Arden, struck by a glass arrow and transformed into ice, shatters upon Drew Prescott's approach.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Nico Arden, struck by a glass arrow, turn into a statue of ice, and then he shattered into frozen shards when Drew Prescott approached.

grounded_facts: After defeating several Eastwood Collective, the Reese Prescott is ambushed from above and pinned down by the upper line of Eastwood Collective.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Reese Prescott rage through the Eastwood Collective, flattening half a dozen of them, but then I watched as Drew Prescott's upper line of Eastwood Collective leapt down from the branches and buried him under their weight.

grounded_facts: A coordinated attack by Eastwood Collective under Drew Prescott's command to capture or eliminate the Reese Prescott near the forest lodge.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the Eastwood Collective under Drew Prescott's command launch a coordinated attack, leaping down from the branches to overwhelm the Reese Prescott near the forest lodge.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne, watching the battle, expresses identification with the Reese Prescott's rage based on a past football experience.
memories.memory_text: I know just how he feels — I remembered our game against the Pittsburgh Steelers last year and saw that same rage in the Reese Prescott.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder instructs Tristan Hawthorne to go inside so she can speak with Drew Prescott alone, asserting control over the situation.
Reese Wilder orders Tristan Hawthorne to go inside, showing dominance and impatience when Tristan Hawthorne hesitates.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Reese Wilder to go inside so she could speak with Drew Prescott alone, and when I hesitated, she snapped at me, calling me a foolish Earthling and demanding that I trust her.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder whispers to Tristan Hawthorne that she is playing a game and that he is merely a toy, signaling her manipulative role.
Reese Wilder tells Tristan Hawthorne she is playing a game, implying she is manipulating others, but leaves her true allegiance unclear.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Wilder whisper in my ear that she was playing a game, and that I was just a toy to her, but I didn't know if she meant it or if it was part of some larger plan.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder asks Drew Prescott to hide Tristan Hawthorne from her father and keep him confined in Arboria.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Wilder ask Drew Prescott to hide me from her father and keep me confined in Arboria.

Drew Prescott mocks Tristan Hawthorne and threatens to kill him after learning of his Eastgate Street origin and Reese Wilder's interest.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Prescott mock me and declare he would hide me under six feet of Arborian dirt, making it clear he intended to kill me.

grounded_facts: A ceremonial confrontation where Drew Prescott plans to execute the captured Reese Prescott and issue a challenge involving a venomous serpent.
Drew Prescott declares his intent to kill the captured Reese Prescott and dedicate his blood to Reese Wilder, defying Micah Hale's authority.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Drew Prescott step forward as his men brought in the netted Reese Prescott, snarling and roaring, and I heard him demand a the black key before declaring he would kill the Reese Prescott and dedicate his blood to Reese Wilder, defying Micah Hale — then later challenge someone to 'dare the beast.'

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott initiates a deadly challenge involving a venomous serpent hidden in a tree stump with six holes.
memories.memory_text: I watched through the door's louvers as Drew Prescott embraced Reese Wilder and then a keeper brought a hissing snake toward a tree stump with six holes; I heard Drew Prescott challenge, 'Who dares the beast?' and saw an old warrior step forward and plunge his hand into one of the holes.

grounded_facts: The old man turns blue and dies after pulling his hand from the stump, indicating the venom's lethal effect.
memories.memory_text: I saw the old man pull his hand from the stump and his face turn blue before Drew Prescott stabbed him and he fell dead.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne asks Reese Wilder to deliver a message to Jonah Vale, expressing regret and love, then retracts it.
memories.memory_text: I asked Reese Wilder to tell Jonah Vale I was sorry and that I loved her, but then I changed my mind and told her to forget it—sending such a message through her felt as foolish as entrusting a lettuce-leaf to a rabbit.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott inserts his hand into one of the remaining holes and is affected by venom, but pretends to be unharmed before showing signs of poisoning.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Prescott glare at me, take a breath, and jam his hand into one of the holes in the stump; his eyes widened and he made a choked sound, then quickly pulled his hand out and forced a grin, pretending he was unharmed even though I could tell something was wrong.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott forces Tristan Hawthorne to choose between inserting his hand into the stump or being killed by the black key.
memories.memory_text: I was forced by Drew Prescott to choose between putting my hand into one of the six openings in the serpent stump—knowing five were safe and one meant death—or being killed by his the black key right then.

grounded_facts: A ritual trial where participants insert their hands into holes in a stump, one of which contains a venomous serpent.
memories.memory_text: I was forced to take part in a trial where I had to put my hand into one of six holes in a stump, knowing one held a venomous serpent that could kill me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne inserts his hand into one of the stump's holes and survives, shifting the psychological balance.
memories.memory_text: I thrust my hand into one of the stump's holes and pulled it out again, knowing I had survived the trial and shifted the balance of power.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne pulls the serpent from the stump instead of being bitten, gaining a weapon.
memories.memory_text: I pulled the serpent from the stump just in time and used it as a weapon, swinging it at the Treemen and thrusting its head toward Drew Prescott to keep him back.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne seizes Drew Prescott's the black key after disarming the serpent, gaining a critical weapon.
memories.memory_text: I seized Drew Prescott's the black key after slamming the serpent's head into the post, making sure I got the weapon before it hit the ground.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne cuts the net binding the Reese Prescott, who then joins him in fighting Eastwood Collective.
memories.memory_text: I slashed the cords of the net to free the Reese Prescott, and then he joined me in fighting off the Eastwood Collective as we raced down the ramp together.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and the Reese Prescott flee the Lodge after Tristan Hawthorne gains the upper hand.
memories.memory_text: After I slammed the serpent's head into the post and grabbed the the black key, I fled the lodge with the Reese Prescott right behind me after I cut him free.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder mocks Drew Prescott's failure by questioning his love and strength.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Wilder mock Drew Prescott, saying something like 'surely the Prince of Arboria wouldn't be beaten by a toy,' questioning his strength and pride after he failed the trial.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott blows a horn to initiate a pursuit of Tristan Hawthorne and the Reese Prescott.
memories.memory_text: I heard Drew Prescott blow a horn as we were escaping, signaling the Eastwood Collective to pursue us.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott thanks Tristan Hawthorne for freeing him, establishing a bond of debt and alliance.
memories.memory_text: I remember Reese Prescott thanking me for freeing him, saying it directly as we started to run.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne questions whether they have any chance of survival, prompting strategic response.
memories.memory_text: I asked Reese Prescott if we had any chance of survival, feeling the weight of our situation.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott reveals that climbing above the green canopy may allow escape from Eastwood Collective, introducing a new survival strategy.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Reese Prescott that we could escape the Eastwood Collective by climbing above the green canopy, giving us a new way forward.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott explains Micah Hale's Law, revealing a strategic weakness in their pursuers.
memories.memory_text: I learned from Reese Prescott about Micah Hale's Law—that outside their kingdom, every hunter becomes the hunted—revealing a weakness in the Eastwood Collective.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott begin fleeing through the forest after freeing Reese Prescott, marking the start of their joint survival effort.
memories.memory_text: I was running through the dense forest with Reese Prescott right after I freed him, and I tripped over a vine but he pulled me up, and we both jumped onto the lowest branch of a huge tree to start climbing.

grounded_facts: A sustained escape sequence through a dense forest involving pursuit, climbing, and confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed our entire escape through the forest—climbing the giant tree like a ladder, never seeing the top, and then spotting a moving vine elevator with a Tree Man in a leafy basket scanning below us.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne kills a Tree Man using a glass arrow, removing an immediate threat and securing access to a vine elevator.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Reese Prescott's crossbow, loaded a glass arrow, and took down the Tree Man just in time to stop him from detecting us.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott board a vertical vine elevator, beginning ascent beyond the known forest.
memories.memory_text: I ran out with Reese Prescott and jumped into the vine elevator basket as it passed, starting our ascent beyond the known forest.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott admits no one has ever been above the green, revealing danger and mystery ahead.
memories.memory_text: Reese Prescott told me that no one has ever been above the green, and I realized how dangerous and unknown the path ahead really is.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott asks Tristan Hawthorne what the color above is.
memories.memory_text: I was asked by Reese Prescott what the color above was.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne names the color above the canopy as 'blue' in response to Reese Prescott's question.
memories.memory_text: I named the color above the canopy as 'blue' when I responded to Reese Prescott.

grounded_facts: Eastwood Collective arrive on a branch, spot Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott, and prepare to attack with crossbows and glass arrows.
memories.memory_text: I saw a dozen Eastwood Collective swing in on vines and land on a fat branch, then I watched them unsling crossbows and grab glass arrows while their Owen Huxley pointed at us and gave a chilling birdcall.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott and his Eastwood Collective change position in the trees to cut off their targets based on a directional signal.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Eastwood Collective swing into view on vines and land on a thick branch, and I noticed their Owen Huxley point right at us and give a chilling birdcall before they unsheathed their crossbows and reached for glass arrows.

grounded_facts: The Tree Man Owen Huxley orders Tristan Hawthorne to drop his weapon.
memories.memory_text: I was told to drop my weapon when the Tree Man Owen Huxley shouted at me, 'You haven't a chance! Throw down your weapon!'

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne pretends to surrender his weapon but instead fires an arrow at the attacking Eastwood Collective.
memories.memory_text: I pretended to throw away my crossbow, but at the last moment I swung it around and fired an arrow at the Eastwood Collective.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne's arrow hits the branch beneath the Eastwood Collective, turning it to ice and causing it to shatter, sending them falling to their doom.
memories.memory_text: I saw my arrow strike the branch beneath the Eastwood Collective, and I watched it instantly turn to ice and shatter, sending them falling.

grounded_facts: A coordinated ambush by Eastwood Collective against Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott in the canopy, which fails due to Tristan Hawthorne's counterattack.
memories.memory_text: I was part of the ambush in the canopy where the Eastwood Collective tried to take me and Reese Prescott down, but I fired an arrow that struck the branch beneath them, turning it to ice and foiling their attack.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne asks Reese Prescott which way leads to the border, seeking navigational guidance.
memories.memory_text: I asked Reese Prescott which way led to the border so we could head in the right direction.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne determines the western direction using his wristwatch and shadow angles to navigate toward the border.
memories.memory_text: I used my wristwatch and the angle of the shadows to figure out which way was west, then started moving.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott traverse the elevated treetop canopy of Arboria, moving toward the western border.
memories.memory_text: I was with Reese Prescott as we jumped into a wide leaf and then ran across bouncy treetop leaves toward the western border of Arboria.

grounded_facts: A fat tendril seizes Tristan Hawthorne mid-air, coils around his waist, and lifts him toward a giant flower's maw.
memories.memory_text: I was bouncing across the leaves when a fat tendril suddenly seized me mid-air, coiled around my waist, and started lifting me toward the flower's maw—I yelled and struggled, realizing with horror it was feeding me into that thing.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott is knocked flat by a tendril while attempting to rescue Tristan Hawthorne.
memories.memory_text: I saw Reese Prescott dash in to rescue me, but a tendril knocked him flat before he could reach me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne is trapped inside the flower with closing petals and deadly spikes, surrounded by skeletons of previous victims.
memories.memory_text: I'm trapped inside this monstrous flower, punching and kicking as the spiny petals close around me, and I can see the crushed skeletons of those who didn't make it out.

grounded_facts: A glass arrow strikes the flower's heart, causing it to shriek and crystallize into ice, releasing Tristan Hawthorne.
The flower's tendrils lose grip due to crystallization, allowing Tristan Hawthorne to fall safely onto a leaf beside the Reese Prescott.
memories.memory_text: I saw a glass arrow fly past my ear and strike the flower's heart, making it shriek and turn into crystalline ice; as the tendrils lost their grip, I fell safely onto a leaf beside the Reese Prescott.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott appears on a leaf with a crossbow, having shot the arrow that saved Tristan Hawthorne, but declares that Tristan Hawthorne's death must be his alone.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Prescott appear on a leaf with his crossbow, and I heard him say that my death must be his alone.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott shoots a glass arrow into the flower, saving Tristan Hawthorne from being crushed, but states that Tristan Hawthorne's death must be his own.
memories.memory_text: I realized Drew Prescott must have shot the glass arrow that saved me when the flower started turning to ice, but he still claimed my death for himself.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott declares that Tristan Hawthorne's death belongs to him alone, rejecting any other outcome.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Drew Prescott that my death belongs to him alone, and he rejected any other outcome.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne questions the purpose of their mutual killing and proposes teaming up to overthrow Micah Hale.
Tristan Hawthorne questions the purpose of killing and suggests teaming up to overthrow Micah Hale.
memories.memory_text: I questioned why we were killing each other and suggested we team up to overthrow Micah Hale instead.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott ignores Tristan Hawthorne's proposal, loads another arrow, and slowly aims at Tristan Hawthorne's heart.
memories.memory_text: I watched Drew Prescott ignore my offer, load another arrow, and slowly aim at my heart.

memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Prescott standing with his crossbow aimed at me, and then a shadow covered him—I looked up and saw a Jamie Warren diving from the sun before it seized him in its talons and carried him into the air.

grounded_facts: Emery Vaughn dive down, seize Tristan Hawthorne and the Reese Prescott, and lift them into the air.
memories.memory_text: After I fell onto the leaf beside the Reese Prescott, I saw Emery Vaughn dive down and seize both me and the Reese Prescott, lifting us into the air.

grounded_facts: A Jamie Warren pretends to release Reese Prescott, who reacts by panicking and retracting his agreement, revealing his fear of falling.
A Jamie Warren sarcastically agrees to release Reese Prescott, causing Reese Prescott to panic and scream 'Nooo!!!' when he realizes he might actually fall.
memories.memory_text: I saw Reese Prescott panic when a Jamie Warren mocked him with a fake release—he screamed 'Nooo!!!' after first saying yes, revealing his terror of falling.

grounded_facts: A group of Redwood Press transport captives through the sky toward and into descent upon a floating Riverside District.
memories.memory_text: I was carried through the sky by Redwood Press, helpless in their grip as we ascended toward a dazzling floating Riverside District high above the clouds.

grounded_facts: The Redwood Press approach and begin descending toward a magnificent airborne Riverside District, marking a transition to a new location of significance.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Redwood Press carrying me, Drew Prescott, and Reese Prescott higher until we rose above the clouds, where a dazzling Riverside District came into view, and then we began a screaming dive toward it.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott is brought to a grand terrace and confronted by Linden Bellamy, who asserts dominance over him.

memories.memory_text: I pushed Jonah Vale into the black lantern to ensure she boarded quickly.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy pushes Jonah Vale into the black lantern, and Tristan Hawthorne follows immediately after.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed myself push Jonah Vale into the black lantern and Tristan Hawthorne following immediately after.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne leaps into the black lantern immediately after Jonah Vale is pushed in.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne leap into the black lantern right after Jonah Vale was inside.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy uses a the glass case to force Tristan Hawthorne into position, asserting control over him.
memories.memory_text: I waved the the glass case at Tristan Hawthorne and told him to sit down and put his foot on the red pedal to assert control.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale encourages Tristan Hawthorne to resist Tristan Quincy's control.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jonah Vale shout 'Tristan Hawthorne! Sack him!' as I was trying to get Tristan Hawthorne into position.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne physically confronts Tristan Quincy in an attempt to stop him.
memories.memory_text: I was slammed back by Tristan Hawthorne after he jumped me and punched me in the gut, trying to stop me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy activates the black lantern's systems, initiating its whirling motion and beginning the launch sequence.
memories.memory_text: I activated the black lantern's systems during the struggle, setting switches in a frenzy and hitting one final switch as I fell to start the whirling motion and launch sequence.

grounded_facts: An unplanned and violent activation of the black lantern involving a struggle and forced entry, leading to rapid spin and launch initiation.
memories.memory_text: After Tristan Hawthorne attacked me, I struggled to maintain control as the black lantern began to whirl and launch unexpectedly.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy reveals the black lantern was built out of friendship and implies a dire global threat.
memories.memory_text: I revealed that I built the black lantern out of friendship and warned that the world is ending unless the three of us can stop it.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy loses consciousness due to extreme G-force after initiating the black lantern's launch.
memories.memory_text: I lost consciousness after launching the black lantern because the G-force became too extreme.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy tries to regain control of the black lantern by operating the control panel, but fails.
memories.memory_text: I tried to regain control of the black lantern by operating the control panel, but when I pushed the switches, nothing happened.

grounded_facts: the black lantern's descent through Harborview Plaza's atmosphere, from initial approach to final hover above a grassy landscape.
the black lantern reaches the planet Harborview Plaza, descending through its fiery surface and a wall of purple vapor before hovering above a grassy landscape.
memories.memory_text: I blinked and struggled to focus, then saw the amber glow of Harborview Plaza's molten surface with flames erupting toward us; I tried to reach the control panel to stop our descent, but the switches didn't respond, and I watched as we passed through a wall of purple vapor and finally slowed above a sea of high grass.

grounded_facts: the black lantern successfully lands on an unknown location, marked by a gentle bump.
memories.memory_text: I felt the gentle bump as our the black lantern touched down, signaling we had landed safely.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy expresses excitement and triumph upon realizing the black lantern has landed successfully.
memories.memory_text: I shouted in triumph, 'By God, we did it! We made it!' because I couldn't contain my excitement that the landing had succeeded.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne questions Tristan Quincy about their location after landing.
memories.memory_text: Tristan Hawthorne turned to me and asked, 'Made it where, Doctor?' right after we landed, putting me on the spot about our location.

grounded_facts: The crew discovers strange men approaching the black lantern after landing.
memories.memory_text: I saw the strange men approaching the black lantern after we landed, and it immediately put me on edge.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale expresses sudden fear and reluctance to leave the black lantern upon seeing the approaching figures.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Jonah Vale suddenly gasp and then say, 'Don't. Suddenly I like it in here just fine,' which made it clear she was afraid to leave.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne attempts to greet the alien Owen Huxley with a handshake, following Tristan Quincy's suggestion, but is instead captured.
memories.memory_text: I told Tristan Hawthorne to extend his hand as a gesture of friendship, believing it would be understood, but the moment he did, the alien Owen Huxley had him seized.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne, Jonah Vale, and Tristan Quincy exit the black lantern and make first contact with the Nico Sinclair.
memories.memory_text: I was with Tristan Hawthorne and Jonah Vale when we exited the black lantern, and I remember the shock of being immediately handcuffed by the Nico Sinclair.

grounded_facts: The first meeting between humans (Tristan Hawthorne, Jonah Vale, Tristan Quincy) and the alien Nico Sinclair on Harborview Plaza.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the first moment humans and the alien Nico Sinclair laid eyes on each other, a tense silence before they suddenly moved to seize us.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne is manacled and thrown to the ground; Jonah Vale and Tristan Quincy are handcuffed and taken prisoner.
memories.memory_text: I was handcuffed along with Jonah Vale after Tristan Hawthorne was manacled and thrown down, and I remember the sudden violence of the Red Men as we were taken prisoner.

grounded_facts: The Owen Huxley declares Tristan Hawthorne and his companions prisoners and announces their transfer to Micah Hale.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Owen Huxley declare us prisoners and say he would take us to Micah Hale.

grounded_facts: After being captured, Tristan Hawthorne sarcastically blames Tristan Quincy for the failed handshake strategy.
memories.memory_text: After we were captured, Tristan Hawthorne lifted his head toward me and said sarcastically, 'Thanks, Doctor -- next time I'll call my own play,' blaming me for the failed handshake strategy.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale publicly tests the loyalty of one of his Tristan Bennett, resulting in the soldier's death.
An armored man kills himself on Micah Hale's command to demonstrate loyalty.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Micah Hale test a soldier's loyalty by asking if he would die for him, and when the armored man said 'Gladly!', I saw him immediately fall on his the black key and impale himself right before our eyes.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne, Jonah Vale, and Tristan Quincy are brought into Micah Hale's Riverside District and confronted by its rulers and customs.
memories.memory_text: I was marched into Micah Hale's Riverside District alongside Tristan Hawthorne and Jonah Vale, overwhelmed by the strange, curving architecture and oppressive atmosphere, and then confronted directly by Micah Hale himself who mocked us as pathetic Earthlings unaware of the true horrors of the universe.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale demands to know who Tristan Hawthorne is and why he has come to Harborview Plaza.
memories.memory_text: I heard Micah Hale demand to know who Tristan Hawthorne was and why he had come to Harborview Plaza.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy expresses interest in studying Evan Nolan's ability to foresee the future.
memories.memory_text: I asked Evan Nolan if his ability to see the future involved a pricking sensation in his temporal lobe, because I was curious about the science behind it.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale orders Tristan Quincy to be chained and preserved for further examination due to his scientific curiosity.
memories.memory_text: I was seized and chained after Micah Hale ordered me preserved for further examination, all because of my curiosity about Evan Nolan.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale declares Tristan Hawthorne useless and orders him killed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Micah Hale declare Tristan Hawthorne useless and order him killed.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale confronts Micah Hale after he orders Tristan Hawthorne's death, daring him to kill her too.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Jonah Vale confront Micah Hale, daring him to kill her too after he ordered Tristan Hawthorne's death.

grounded_facts: Reese Wilder whispers to Micah Hale, asking him to spare Tristan Hawthorne and give him to her instead of killing him.
memories.memory_text: I saw Reese Wilder whisper to Micah Hale, asking him not to kill Tristan Hawthorne and to give him to her instead.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale defends herself by incapacitating a hooded guard with a kick.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Vale defend herself by kicking a hooded guard and taking him down fast.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne overcomes his hesitation and attacks Amazon Noel Keaton to protect Jonah Vale.
memories.memory_text: I watched Tristan Hawthorne hesitate at first, but then he made up his mind and attacked the Amazon Noel Keaton to protect Jonah Vale.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy is being escorted by Tristan Bennett through the cavern, heavily shackled, indicating his prisoner status.
memories.memory_text: I was being led through the cavern by Tristan Bennett, my limbs weighed down by heavy shackles, and I knew I was their prisoner.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy expresses awe at being in the core of the planet, indicating a significant realization or recognition of their location.
memories.memory_text: I realized we were at the very core of the planet, and I said aloud, 'Incredible - the very core of this planet, is it not?'

grounded_facts: Micah Hale responds to Tristan Quincy's remark, confirming his correct guess about their location.
memories.memory_text: I heard Micah Hale respond to me, saying, 'You guess well, Tristan Quincy!' which told me I was right about our location.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy turns in his chains and looks up upon hearing Micah Hale, indicating a physical and attentional response.
memories.memory_text: I turned in my chains and looked up when I heard Micah Hale, directing my attention toward him.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy condemns Micah Hale for using advanced science for destruction rather than peace, suggesting that Micah Hale's legacy could have been positive.
memories.memory_text: I condemned Micah Hale, telling him he should use his science for peace — I said his name could be blessed instead of cursed.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale tells Tristan Quincy that he will use Jonah Vale to repopulate Eastgate Street, invoking the myth of Adam and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I was told directly by Micah Hale that he would use Jonah Vale to create new life, saying he’d done it on over a thousand planets, and that he saw himself as a god recreating Adam and Eve.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale declares his intention to breed with Jonah Vale and repopulate Eastgate Street in his image, referencing Adam and Eve.
memories.memory_text: I gasped when I realized Micah Hale intended to breed with Jonah Vale and repopulate Eastgate Street in his image, invoking the myth of Adam and Eve as if it justified his monstrous plan.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale demonstrates a holographic simulation of Eastgate Street's past, future destruction, and rebirth using a plasma-powered device.
A controlled presentation by Micah Hale in his dome, showing Tristan Quincy the fate of Eastgate Street and his grand reproductive plan.
memories.memory_text: I stood in chains before Micah Hale, watching in horror as he used a plasma-powered device to project a holographic Eastgate Street that was consumed by fire and then vanished at his command—he showed me this to demonstrate his control over Eastgate Street's fate and his grand plan.

grounded_facts: Micah Hale mocks Tristan Quincy's attempt to draw a the black key, stating it is reserved for him or his heir.
memories.memory_text: I heard Micah Hale mock me, saying the the black key were not for my kind and that only he or his rightful heir could draw them, as if to emphasize my powerlessness.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy tries to pull one of the swords from the crystal block but fails; Micah Hale states only he or his heir can remove them.
memories.memory_text: I lunged at the crystal block and seized one of the the black key hilts, pulling with all my strength, but it wouldn't budge no matter how hard I tried, and I collapsed, panting, over the stone.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale discloses being naked in a bathtub, under preparation for Micah Hale, with Tristan Quincy imprisoned.
memories.memory_text: I was told Jonah Vale is naked in a bathtub, being prepared for Micah Hale, and that I'm imprisoned in a dungeon, chained.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne reacts with alarm upon hearing Jonah Vale is with Reese Wilder, calling her a 'bitch' and warning not to trust her.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne react with alarm when he learned Jonah Vale was with Reese Wilder, calling her a 'bitch' and warning not to trust her.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne tells Jonah Vale to deceive Micah Hale's forces and free Tristan Quincy while promising future rescue.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Jonah Vale would try to deceive Micah Hale's forces and get to me to set me free, and that Tristan Hawthorne would find a way to help later.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne expresses longing and romantic commitment, implying shared thoughts and future reunion.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne swear he'd find Jonah Vale and that they'd reunite, no matter what.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale pretends to flirt with the guard to distract him before attacking.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jonah Vale pretends to flirt with the guard to distract him before attacking.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale, disguised as a Drew Carver, incapacitates a guard and obtains the keys to free Tristan Quincy from his chains.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jonah Vale, disguised as a Drew Carver, incapacitates a guard and obtains the keys to free Tristan Quincy from his chains.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale asks Tristan Quincy if the black lantern will fly, expressing concern about their ability to proceed with the rescue mission.
memories.memory_text: I was asked if the black lantern will fly, and I could hear the concern in Jonah Vale's voice about whether we could proceed with the rescue mission.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy reports that the basic circuits of the black lantern appear functional.
memories.memory_text: I checked the systems and reported that the basic circuits of the black lantern seem okay, which meant we might be able to get it working.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale emphasizes that the black lantern must fly because they need to rescue Tristan Hawthorne from the vampire immediately.
memories.memory_text: I was told the black lantern has to fly because we need to rescue Tristan Hawthorne from the vampire immediately, and I understood how urgent it was.

grounded_facts: A sudden blinding blue light explodes within the black lantern, marking a critical and unexpected event during the activation process.
memories.memory_text: I saw a sudden blinding blue light explode inside the black lantern, and I knew we were in immediate danger.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale gasps and reacts with shock upon seeing that Tristan Quincy's hands are invisible.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Vale gasp and exclaim, 'My God -- your hands! Your hands are gone!' when she saw my invisible hands.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy's hands suddenly become invisible after the black lantern lands, though he can still use them physically.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my hands had suddenly become invisible after the black lantern landed, though I could still move and use them.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy hypothesizes that Harborview Plaza's gravitational field reversed his generator's polarity, causing the invisibility.
memories.memory_text: I believe Harborview Plaza's gravitational field reversed the polarity of my generator, causing the invisibility.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy's invisible hands gradually become visible again.
memories.memory_text: I saw my hands slowly fading back into view, becoming visible again right before my eyes.

grounded_facts: Redwood Press descend and carry off Tristan Quincy and Jonah Vale into the air, mirroring previous abductions.
memories.memory_text: I was suddenly seized by the Redwood Press as they swooped down and carried me and Jonah Vale aloft, just like they did with Tristan Hawthorne and Reese Prescott.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale is captured and taken to the eyrie by the Redwood Press, where she is threatened by Hawkgirls.
memories.memory_text: I heard that Jonah Vale was taken to the eyrie by the Redwood Press and threatened by jealous Hawkgirls who pushed her toward the edge.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne catches Jonah Vale as she falls past the terrace and pulls her to safety.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne catch Jonah Vale as she fell past the terrace and pull her to safety, where they embraced.

grounded_facts: A formal movement led by Linden Bellamy through the Riverside District, involving Tristan Hawthorne, Jonah Vale, Tristan Quincy, and others, escorted by Redwood Press toward a ceremonial terrace.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a formal procession led by Linden Bellamy through the Riverside District, escorted by Redwood Press toward a ceremonial terrace.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale expresses fear and homesickness, urging Tristan Hawthorne not to continue, reflecting her emotional distress.
memories.memory_text: I heard Jonah Vale express her fear and homesickness, pleading with Tristan Hawthorne not to continue, which showed how deeply distressed she was.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne resolves to continue with the procession, indicating he feels compelled by Harborview Plaza's ways, despite Jonah Vale's emotional plea to stop.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne resolve to continue with the procession, saying he had to go on, indicating he felt bound by Harborview Plaza's way despite Jonah Vale's plea.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne silently comforts Jonah Vale by squeezing her hand, signaling solidarity despite the tension.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Tristan Hawthorne silently comfort Jonah Vale by squeezing her hand, showing solidarity even in the midst of tension.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne provokes Drew Prescott by linking his defeat to the impossibility of winning Reese Wilder while Micah Hale lives.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne challenge Drew Prescott, telling him that even if he won, he'd never have Reese Wilder as long as Micah Hale lived.

grounded_facts: A formal or spontaneous combat between Tristan Hawthorne and Drew Prescott on a dangerous, tilting disc, witnessed by allies and enemies alike.
memories.memory_text: I watched as Tristan Hawthorne and Drew Prescott began their duel on a greased, tilting disc, lashing at each other while the platform swayed beneath them.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale shouts her love for Tristan Hawthorne and urges him to win, boosting his determination.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Jonah Vale shout to Tristan Hawthorne that she loved him and urge him to win, which clearly strengthened his resolve.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne overcomes Drew Prescott in a duel on a tilting, greased disc, flipping him over the edge and holding his life in his hands.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne overcome Drew Prescott in the fight, flipping him over the edge and then grabbing his wrist, holding him above the abyss.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy uses Tristan Hawthorne's act of saving Drew Prescott to critique Linden Bellamy's lack of compassion.
memories.memory_text: I told Linden Bellamy to call it what he wants—compassion or mercy—and that we should teach him the meaning of these words, using Tristan Hawthorne's rescue as an example.

grounded_facts: Despite winning the duel, Tristan Hawthorne rescues Drew Prescott from falling into the abyss, demonstrating mercy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne catch Drew Prescott just as he was about to fall into the abyss, and I heard Tristan Hawthorne gasp, 'Try to catch my wrist! -- the other one,' then urge him, 'Swing your body -- see if you can get a leg up here!'

grounded_facts: Micah Hale demands Linden Bellamy kill Tristan Hawthorne and deliver Jonah Vale, threatening to destroy his kingdom otherwise.
Micah Hale commands Linden Bellamy to kill Tristan Hawthorne and deliver Jonah Vale, threatening destruction of his kingdom.
memories.memory_text: I heard Micah Hale demand that Linden Bellamy kill Tristan Hawthorne and deliver Jonah Vale, threatening to destroy his kingdom if he refused.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy confronts Linden Bellamy with a moral choice: death or dishonor.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Linden Bellamy with a choice between death and dishonor, hoping to push him toward a decision.

grounded_facts: A critical standoff at the Riverside District where Linden Bellamy is pressured by Micah Hale and ultimately decides to rebel, while Drew Prescott is rescued.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the standoff at the Riverside District where Micah Hale confronted Linden Bellamy, and I saw Linden Bellamy make the decision to rebel and save the Earthlings.

grounded_facts: After being challenged by Tristan Quincy, Linden Bellamy decides to defy Micah Hale and orders his Crown Hill Medical Center to save the Earthlings.
memories.memory_text: After I challenged him, I saw Linden Bellamy make up his mind and order his Crown Hill Medical Center to save the Earthlings, defying Micah Hale.

grounded_facts: After deciding to rebel, Linden Bellamy refuses Tristan Quincy's offered hand, expressing confusion.
memories.memory_text: I offered my hand to Linden Bellamy after he decided to rebel, but he just looked at it and said he didn't understand, like he was losing his mind.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Jonah Vale exchange loving glances and playful romantic banter while flying.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed Tristan Hawthorne and Jonah Vale exchanging loving glances and playful romantic banter while they were flown about a hundred feet apart, with Tristan Hawthorne saying they’d do something important right after landing.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne shouts to Jonah Vale that he is coming to save her after she is captured.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne shout, 'I'm coming, Jonah Vale!' as he tried to reach her after she was captured.

grounded_facts: A squadron of Redwood Press carries the protagonists in flight toward cloud cover, en route to retrieving the black lantern.
memories.memory_text: I was carried by a Jamie Warren as part of a squadron flying toward cloud cover, en route to retrieving my the black lantern while distant explosions rumbled below.

grounded_facts: Following Linden Bellamy's order, the Redwood Press begin a vertical dive, abandoning pursuit of Jonah Vale.
Tristan Hawthorne orders his Jamie Warren to follow and rescue Jonah Vale, but is forced into a dive due to Linden Bellamy's command.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne order his Jamie Warren to follow and climb to rescue Jonah Vale, but then Linden Bellamy gave a command and we were forced into a vertical dive, abandoning the pursuit.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy is inside the black lantern, actively re-wiring a control panel in urgent manner.
memories.memory_text: I am inside the black lantern, feverishly re-wiring the control panel to get the spacecraft ready for launch.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy calls out to Tristan Hawthorne, announcing that he is ready to begin a test, interrupting the meeting.
memories.memory_text: I called out to Tristan Hawthorne, announcing I was ready to begin the test and interrupting their meeting.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy directs Tristan Hawthorne to sit and wait for a signal to press a button, establishing a coordinated action sequence.
Tristan Quincy tells Tristan Hawthorne to sit and press a button when given the signal 'zero'.
memories.memory_text: I told Tristan Hawthorne to sit and wait for my signal 'zero' before pressing the button, so we could execute the action sequence at the right moment.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy counts down and activates the black lantern, resulting in a burst of blinding blue light.
memories.memory_text: I counted down and activated the black lantern, and there was a burst of blinding blue light.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy checks if Tristan Hawthorne is inside and tells him he can come out after the activation.
memories.memory_text: I checked if Tristan Hawthorne was inside and called out to him, asking if he could hear me and where he was, so he could come out after the activation.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne shouts from inside the black lantern, telling Tristan Quincy to move so he can exit.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne shout from inside the black lantern, telling me to get out of his way so he could exit.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne emerges from the black lantern completely invisible, though his shadow is visible on the ground.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne emerge from the black lantern completely invisible, though I could clearly see his shadow on the ground as he stood up.

grounded_facts: A rising whining humming sound fills the sky, the Eastgate Street trembles, and brown smoking foliage rains down, causing fear among the inhabitants.
memories.memory_text: I heard a rising whining humming sound fill the sky, felt the Eastgate Street tremble beneath me, and saw brown, smoking foliage rain down as Crown Hill Medical Center around me cowered in fear.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott questions Tristan Quincy about the catastrophic environmental effects following the black lantern activation.
memories.memory_text: Drew Prescott turned to me and shouted, 'Tristan Quincy! What have you done?' as if I were responsible for the catastrophe following the black lantern activation.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan descends in a shuttle craft and confronts the group, demanding to know Tristan Hawthorne's location.
Evan Nolan directly questions Tristan Quincy about Tristan Hawthorne's whereabouts, asserting authority.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan descend in a shuttle craft and confront us, then he walked straight to me and demanded to know where Tristan Hawthorne was.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy informs Evan Nolan that Tristan Hawthorne is dead after being dropped by his Jamie Warren.
memories.memory_text: I told Evan Nolan that Tristan Hawthorne was dead after being dropped by his Jamie Warren.

grounded_facts: The dungeon door opens by itself, indicating external intervention or hidden mechanism activation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the dungeon door open by itself, which meant someone or something outside had triggered a mechanism.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne calls out to the captives, signaling arrival or rescue attempt.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne calling out to us captives, saying 'It's me!', letting us know he had arrived.

grounded_facts: Drew Prescott, Tristan Quincy, Reese Prescott, and Tristan Hawthorne are climbing up a narrow vertical shaft in back-to-back pairs, using their feet against the walls for support.
memories.memory_text: I was climbing up a narrow vertical shaft with Drew Prescott, Reese Prescott, and Tristan Hawthorne, moving slowly in back-to-back pairs and using our feet against the walls for support.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne explains that an anti-gravity shaft can be used to reach the plasma level, having been shown by a guard earlier.
memories.memory_text: I heard Tristan Hawthorne say that an anti-gravity shaft can be used to reach the plasma level, after a guard showed it to him.

grounded_facts: The plasma is contracting into a critical mass, indicating imminent destruction of Eastgate Street when the needle reaches the red zone.
memories.memory_text: I saw the plasma contracting into a critical mass and told the others that when the needle hits the red zone, Eastgate Street is finished.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott declares he will charge down at the enemies, but is met with silence and stares, causing him to abandon his stance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Reese Prescott declare he would charge down at the enemies, but when Drew Prescott and I just looked at him, he slumped out of his stance.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy concedes defeat, acknowledging that without a miracle, they have lost.
memories.memory_text: I let go of hope and told my friends that without a miracle, we've lost.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne overrides the discussion about future targets to insist on prioritizing the cavern and Tristan Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I was told that the cavern had to come first and that I was needed there urgently.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy turns his face away from the glare of the slot-window, expressing deep sorrow.
memories.memory_text: I turned my face away from the harsh glare of the slot-window, overwhelmed by sorrow as the weight of our doomed history pressed upon me.

grounded_facts: Reese Prescott, positioned at the window, calls out after noticing something significant outside.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Prescott call out suddenly from the window, alerting us to something he had spotted outside.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy, Drew Prescott, and Reese Prescott urgently move toward the low exit in the crawlspace.
memories.memory_text: I scrambled toward the low exit with Drew Prescott and Reese Prescott, moving fast to get out.

grounded_facts: A battle between Redwood Press and Jonah Sinclair slaves and Micah Hale's Crown Hill Medical Center takes place in the Plasma Cavern.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the battle between the Redwood Press and Jonah Sinclair slaves against Micah Hale's Crown Hill Medical Center while fighting alongside Linden Bellamy and Reese Prescott to reach the Mezzanine Control area.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy shouts instructions to attach electrodes to shovels and throw them into the plasma.
memories.memory_text: I shouted the command to attach electrodes to the shovels and throw them into the plasma.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy flips a switch after making urgent repairs to a wiring panel, potentially triggering a critical system response.
memories.memory_text: I flipped the switch after making urgent repairs to the wiring panel, knowing it might trigger a critical response from the system.

grounded_facts: Redwood Press, Tristan Bennett, and former Eastwood Press tend to the wounded in a moment of peace after conflict.
memories.memory_text: I saw Redwood Press, Tristan Bennett, and former Eastwood Press tending to the wounded, bringing peace after the battle.

grounded_facts: Jonah Vale expresses sorrow over losing the black lantern, realizing they can never return to Eastgate Street, but Tristan Quincy reframes their presence on Harborview Plaza as being home.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Jonah Vale that she felt we could never return to Eastgate Street, and I realized she was grieving our displacement.

grounded_facts: Tristan Quincy tells Jonah Vale that they are already home, offering emotional comfort after her realization of displacement.
memories.memory_text: I told Jonah Vale that we are already home, hoping to comfort her in that moment of sorrow.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne and Tristan Quincy affirm that their current location, Harborview Plaza, is now their true home.
memories.memory_text: I affirmed to Jonah Vale and Tristan Hawthorne that we are home here on Harborview Plaza, and Tristan Hawthorne agreed with me.

grounded_facts: Tristan Hawthorne kisses Jonah Vale after she laughs at Tristan Quincy's suggestion of their honeymoon, affirming their relationship.
memories.memory_text: I saw Tristan Hawthorne kiss Jonah Vale after she laughed at my suggestion about their honeymoon, and I knew their bond was truly affirmed.

memories.memory_text: I remember the plane jolting hard, nearly knocking my karate book out of my hand, and how I automatically tossed my hair out of my eyes—same thing I always do when I'm scared.
I snapped at Tristan Hawthorne to shut up when the plane was shaking—there was no time for his suggestions, not when the pilots were already struggling to keep us in the air.

I snapped at Tristan Hawthorne when he offered me a candy bar—like I’d take sweets from a stranger—but then I couldn’t help it, I asked if I could still have it after admitting how much I hate flying.
I gasped when I realized the plane might be moving backward—then I saw the clouds rushing past and shouted, 'Holy cow! Look at the clouds!'—it felt like we were falling.
I remember the light—cold and strange—washing over my face, and I couldn't speak, couldn't move, just clung to Tristan Hawthorne's hand like it was the only real thing left.
I remember stumbling into the cockpit, the wind tearing at me like a living thing, and seeing Tristan Hawthorne fighting the controls as the plane plunged downward.
As we strained on the yoke together, I cracked that joke about the man falling ninety stories—Tristan Hawthorne didn’t know it, and for a second, the terror felt lighter.
I recognized him from a Crown Hill Medical Center article after he left NASA — something about him being unstable, and the way he was smiling just confirmed it.
He pressed the the glass case into my back and I felt the heat from those red laser bolts — I couldn't move, I just ran when he shoved me toward the stairs.

I gasped and shrank back when Tristan Quincy ripped open that shiny Stonebridge Warehouse and pointed his the glass case at us, yelling about dying in space — then he shoved me inside like I didn’t even matter.
I shouted at Tristan Hawthorne to take Tristan Quincy down—he was forcing us into this thing like a madman, and I couldn’t just sit there.
The spinning got so strong I was crushed against Tristan Hawthorne, my back pressed to his chest—I couldn’t move, barely breathe, like the force was molding us together.
I remember clinging to Tristan Hawthorne as we tumbled through that hellish fire—my head spinning, the world just a blur of amber and flame, and then that sudden, impossible rise above the lava.
I remember the cold snap of the manacle locking around my wrist, the red Nico Sinclair moving fast—no warning, just hands grabbing me, pulling me down as if I were nothing.
I caught a glimpse of that poor man's torn body and the beast being tormented—then I shut my eyes tight and tried to pretend we were on a stupid vacation to Disneyland instead.

I fought hard, kicking and striking with everything I had, but there were too many of them — I remember the cold grip of their hands dragging me up the stairs, screaming Tristan Hawthorne’s name into the dark.
I was reaching down, straining to hold Tristan Hawthorne's hand—our fingertips just barely touched, and for a second, I thought I could pull him up.
I saw the step beneath Tristan Hawthorne open like a mouth and swallow him whole—he screamed and then vanished, and that woman Reese Wilder jumped in after him before the door snapped shut.
I remember the fear creeping in when I realized Micah Hale might force me into marriage—becoming his consort wasn't rescue, it was another kind of prison.
I knocked the flagon out of her hand with a karate chop when she tried to make me drink that green stuff—like hell I’d just obey them.
I screamed for Tristan Hawthorne, but no one answered—and then I just broke, grabbed the flagon and drank it, surprised at how good it tasted.
Tristan Hawthorne asked Reese Wilder to let him use the thought-transfer device to contact me, and said 'Please' when she teased him about not showing him how.

I was sitting naked in that bathtub, feeling completely exposed, when Tristan Hawthorne’s voice suddenly came into my head—telling me to fake compliance and free Tristan Quincy before Micah Hale could get to me.
When Tristan Hawthorne asked if I could get what he was thinking, I said yes. I understood him without words.
I smiled and told her I was ready, then waited until she leaned over the bed—when her guard was down, I struck fast with a karate-chop to make sure she wouldn’t interfere.

Shawn Vale walked in smiling, holding yards of white fabric, and said, 'Your wedding dress'—I froze, not knowing whether to scream or run.
I walked down the hall on Evan Nolan's arm, the Eastwood Press prodding me forward, their spears at my back, while girls carried my train and Micah Hale stared at me like I was already his.

memories.memory_text: I was going over a play in my head when the plane jolted hard—next thing I knew, I was on my feet, leaning into the cockpit to check on the pilots.

I grabbed the rack above Jonah Vale when the plane jolted, then sat beside her and offered my candy bar—she shot me a look like I was some creep, but I told her I wasn't a stranger, not with my face on Crown Hill Medical Center.
She asked if we were going backward, then gasped and pointed at the clouds—her voice was tight with fear, and I could feel the plane lurching, something wasn't right.
The sky turned red and the clouds started moving impossibly fast around the plane — I could feel Jonah Vale squeezing my hand like she was afraid she'd vanish.
I remember the cockpit door exploding open, wind tearing through the cabin, papers flying everywhere—I was on my feet in an instant, unbuckling and moving forward fast.
I lunged into the cockpit and grabbed the bucking yoke, fighting to pull the plane out of the dive as wind tore through the shattered windows.
Jonah Vale shouted some dumb joke about a man falling ninety stories while we were both yanking the controls, and for a second it cut through the panic—I actually wanted to hear how it ended.
I shouted to brace ourselves—I was locking onto that field up ahead as the only shot we had to land this thing.

I remember Jonah Vale suddenly stopping, staring at Tristan Quincy like she’d seen a ghost, and then trying to back out fast—something about a magazine, NASA, and almost saying he was insane. I didn’t get it at first, but her look told me everything.

One second we were talking, the next—Tristan Quincy pulls a the glass case and shoves it into Jonah Vale’s back, yelling about Eastgate Street being attacked. Red laser bolts are exploding the greenhouse around us, glass raining down, fire everywhere, and he’s jabbing me with the the glass case, screaming 'Up the stairs—RUN!'
I saw Tristan Quincy shove Jonah Vale into that mirror-bright Stonebridge Warehouse and I didn't think—I just leapt after her, the world exploding around us.
I jumped Tristan Quincy, punched him in the gut, and tried to stop him from launching, but he slammed me back and hit a switch that made the black lantern start whirling.
The spinning got worse, I grabbed Jonah Vale and held her close as the force slammed us against the wall—our bodies pressed together, barely able to move.

I remember holding Jonah Vale as we crashed through the fire, the black lantern spinning, then slowing—my arms were locked around her, and when I saw Harborview Plaza’s molten surface rushing up, I thought we were dead.
I stepped forward, smiled, and said 'Hi!'—reaching out my hand like it was a normal first meeting, but the next thing I knew, a manacle snapped onto my wrist and I was slammed to the ground.

I grabbed Tristan Quincy and shouted in his face—'You got us into this—HOW DO WE GET OUT?'—because we were being dragged through some twisted hall by armored goons and he was still yammering about Black Holes like it was a damn science fair.

I don’t know what Micah Hale said next, but the way those Nico Sinclair tightened their grip and the air went cold—I knew they were about to execute us. I locked eyes with him, ready to fight even if it was the last thing I did.
I was on the floor, completely overwhelmed—dozens of Eastwood Press on top of me, pressing me down, and I could see Jonah Vale being dragged up the stairs, helpless.
I heard her scream my name—'Tristan Hawthorne!!'—and something inside me snapped; I just exploded upward and broke free, charging after her.
I was so close to Jonah Vale—our fingertips just brushed—and then the step beneath me vanished, and I was falling, screaming into the dark.

I was falling through this dark, endless shaft, and all I could hear was Reese Wilder yelling to take a breath and grab her ankle when we hit the water—then suddenly, a massive splash swallowed everything.

I saw it through the glass—the lake of seething magma, glowing like hell itself, spinning slow and hot, feeding that weapon aimed at Eastgate Street. Reese Wilder said it was the plasma core, unstoppable, but I knew we had to try.

The Jonah Sinclair—chained, shoveling gravel into the magma, Noel Keaton shocking them when they fall. If they couldn't get up, those hooded men just threw them in. I saw one collapse… and vanish into the fire.

I grabbed Reese Wilder’s shoulders and demanded to know where Jonah Vale was—then she pulled me into a niche as Valerie Thorne passed, her body pressed against mine, and whispered that Micah Hale intends to marry Jonah Vale. I could barely process it—Micah Hale marrying Jonah Vale? It hit me like a shock I couldn’t shake.

I looked through the glass doors and saw rocket ships inside—real ones—and when Reese Wilder said I’d fly them, I snapped, 'I can’t fly a damn rocket ship!' Her teasing reply barely registered; all I could think was this mission just got a thousand times riskier.
I asked Reese Wilder why the moon kingdoms don’t team up against Micah Hale, and then it hit me—what if they could? That moment, I saw it: not just fighting, but uniting as a real strategy.

I slammed my hand on the controls, sent the ship into a dive—Reese Wilder screamed, dropped the telepathic hood. I grabbed her wrists before she could stop me. I had to force her to let me reach Jonah Vale.

I had to hold Reese Wilder's wrists tight—she was fighting me, but I couldn't let go until she connected me to Jonah Vale. The planet was rushing up at us, but I didn't care—I wasn't losing her again.
I told Jonah Vale to fake them out and get to Tristan Quincy—she was scared, chained up and about to be handed over to Micah Hale, but she had to move fast and stay sharp.

When she said she was naked in a bathtub, I couldn't breathe—my voice broke, and for a second all I wanted was to touch her; then I just held on to the thought that she understood me, even without words.
I stared into Reese Wilder's eyes and almost sent Jonah Vale a final message, but then I realized it was pointless—sending words through her would be like handing a lettuce-leaf to a rabbit.

I jammed my hand into one of the serpent stump's holes, left it just long enough to make everyone think the worst, then yanked it out and threw the challenge back at Drew Prescott—'Your turn, Drew Prescott.'

I called out to Jonah Vale mid-flight, telling her we were gonna do it first thing when we landed—she smiled and said I’d make her blush, like we had time for shyness with everything falling apart around us.

One second she was there, then a shadow fell over her—next thing I saw was that glow pulling her and her Jamie Warren up into a ship; I screamed 'I'm coming, Jonah Vale!' and told my Jamie Warren to climb, but he dove instead.
I climbed out of the black lantern and heard Drew Prescott shout that I was casting a shadow—completely invisible, but my shadow was still there on the ground.
I snatched the ring from Micah Hale’s hand and slammed it onto Jonah Vale’s finger—her gasp cut through the silence, and for a heartbeat, I knew she felt me there.
I drew the the black key from the crystal block and held it before me. When it appeared like fire, Micah Hale reacted sharply and said only his heir could pull it.
